vibe: A patch-now security morning: PHP, Node.js, GitLab and network gear all demand attention, while agent isolation is becoming a real cloud design discipline.

cyber.title: PHP2Shell Exploit Attempts Hit Millions as Attackers Try to Deploy Mirai Malware
cyber.summary: PHP2Shell scanning has surged into the millions, with attackers trying to turn exposed PHP servers into Mirai bots. Treat the emergency PHP updates as an internet-facing patch-now event; mitigations are only a stopgap.

cyber.title: PHP shares mitigation for new RCE vulnerability with no patch
cyber.summary: PHP has disclosed a second remote-code-execution risk with no patch yet. Operators should apply the vendor mitigation immediately, reduce exposure, and watch for revised packages.

cyber.title: HPE patches eight max severity RCE and auth bypass AOS flaws
cyber.summary: HPE has fixed eight maximum-severity flaws in Aruba AOS devices, including remote-code execution and authentication bypasses. Network teams should inventory affected gear and prioritize the vendor updates.

cyber.title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
cyber.summary: Researchers found exposed attacker infrastructure showing ransomware affiliates using AI agents during intrusions. It is useful operational evidence that agentic tooling is moving from speculation into real offensive workflows.

cyber.title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
cyber.summary: A crafted Brotli stream can trigger a practical Node.js remote-code-execution chain dubbed Node2Shell. Node operators should check affected releases and update rather than relying on input filtering.

cyber.title: Ruby Fixes Three Regex Engine Bugs Responsible for Four Critical GitLab RCE Flaws
cyber.summary: Ruby fixed three regular-expression engine bugs that underpin four critical GitLab RCE vulnerabilities. GitLab administrators should ensure both application and runtime fixes are accounted for.

cyber.title: BlackX UEFI Bootkit Bypasses Secure Boot on Patched Windows Systems Missing Revocations
cyber.summary: The BlackX UEFI bootkit can bypass Secure Boot where systems are patched but revocation data is stale. Windows fleets need firmware and Secure Boot revocation hygiene, not OS updates alone.

cyber.title: Microsoft Links Storm-0940 to ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
cyber.summary: Microsoft has attributed the ConnectWise supply-chain compromise to Storm-0940. Review ConnectWise exposure, credentials and downstream access, because supply-chain footholds tend to fan out quietly.

cyber.title: Russia-Linked Hackers Used New Mesh Network Backdoor in Destructive Ukraine Attack
cyber.summary: A Russia-linked group used a new mesh-network backdoor in a destructive attack against Ukraine. The peer-to-peer design is notable because it makes command infrastructure harder to disrupt and detect.

cyber.title: Quest Diagnostics confirms data breach exposed patient records
cyber.summary: Quest Diagnostics says an intrusion exposed patient personal and health information. The sensitivity of medical data makes follow-on phishing and identity abuse the practical risk to watch.

cyber.title: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts
cyber.summary: Capcom says 11.7 million accounts were exposed and is warning users about phishing. Reused credentials and convincing game-themed lures are the likely near-term fallout.

ai.title: Google Cloud Launches Agent Compute Engine: A MicroVM per AI Agent
ai.summary: Google Cloud has introduced Agent Compute Engine, isolating each AI agent in its own microVM. The design is directly relevant to cloud engineers wrestling with agent permissions, containment and reproducible execution.

ai.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
ai.summary: Anthropic argues that language models can scale formal software verification by helping translate intent into proofs and specifications. It is a meaningful bridge between AI coding assistance and stronger correctness guarantees.

ai.title: Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
ai.summary: Canva's in-house model separates design planning from image generation, aiming for more coherent layouts rather than merely attractive pixels. That planning-first architecture is the interesting part.

ai.title: Microsoft Teams to get AI-powered, context-aware phishing detection
ai.summary: Teams is adding context-aware phishing detection that uses AI to assess messages and surrounding signals. It could reduce collaboration-platform phishing, but administrators should treat it as another control rather than a substitute for policy.

it.title: Torvalds: AI is fine for competent devs, but spare us the 'drive-by' patches
it.summary: Linus Torvalds says AI-assisted contributions can be useful when competent developers remain accountable, while low-effort drive-by patches create review burden. The message is governance and ownership, not blanket rejection.

it.title: OpenSSL 4.1.0
it.summary: OpenSSL 4.1.0 is out. Infrastructure teams should review the release notes and compatibility implications before rolling it through distributions and dependent services.

it.title: Does Your Model Run on AWS Trainium? Look It Up
it.summary: Hugging Face has published a compatibility lookup for models on AWS Trainium. It is a handy planning aid for teams evaluating lower-cost accelerator options without guessing at framework support.

it.title: The Regression Tests Nobody Writes: Capturing How Software Actually Behaves
it.summary: A practical argument for capturing observed production behavior as regression tests, especially when documentation and intended behavior diverge. Useful engineering reading for safer refactors and AI-assisted changes.

videos.title: The most vulnerable week in internet history...
videos.verdict: WATCH — fast, useful synthesis of the week's patching emergencies.
videos.summary: Fireship connects PHP2Shell, a compromised high-download Python package, long-lived GitLab bugs and certificate-authority failures into one sharp infrastructure-risk roundup.

videos.title: MLB uses Gemini on Google Cloud to field technical ballpark network alerts
videos.verdict: WATCH — short, concrete cloud-operations case study.
videos.summary: MLB built a Gemini-based connectivity agent that checks ballpark network faults and opens correctly routed provider tickets, replacing hundreds of manual tickets and saving minutes to an hour per incident.

videos.title: Self-replicating AI, your doctor’s chatbot & agents at dinner
videos.verdict: SKIM — the agent-security opening is the strongest segment.
videos.summary: IBM's panel covers research on small models replicating across edge devices, risks from clinical chatbots, and agent-to-agent interaction. The useful takeaway is that local agents enlarge the attack surface even without a data-centre connection.

videos.title: AI Home Security Threat
videos.verdict: SKIM — a concise warning about prompt-injection paths from email into privileged home agents.
videos.summary: The immediate risk is not a science-fiction robot revolt but a local agent reading a malicious email, being hijacked, and then acting through insecure smart-home devices.

videos.title: AI and the Holy Organ: Inside Neurosurgery at Johns Hopkins | Amazon Web Services
videos.verdict: SKIM — useful healthcare-AI context, but partly AWS showcase.
videos.summary: Johns Hopkins clinicians discuss using AI to reduce documentation and coordination load so surgeons can focus on care, while stressing precision and responsibility in high-stakes medicine.

videos.title: The New Industrialists | How SymphonyAI Takes Industrial Intelligence Beyond the Pilot
videos.verdict: SKIM — relevant enterprise pattern, but vendor-heavy.
videos.summary: SymphonyAI describes layering industrial context and applications over Microsoft's cloud data and AI stack, with the focus on measurable manufacturing outcomes rather than isolated pilots.
